operations_plan.summary: Establish the hook-lock layout and create a compact transverse-axis hinge support at the root of the existing open hook.

steps.description: Inspect the positive-X hook region and construct a local reference system with the XZ mid-plane at y=0 as the gate motion plane and a prospective hinge axis parallel to Y. Measure the hook-mouth span from the upper hook-root/neck region to the retaining nose, the local Y thickness, and the available material outside the radius-3 mm throat surfaces. Preserve the radius-3 mm load seat, radius-9 mm outer hook body, and existing nose height at z=15 mm. No lock type, load rating, material, manufacturing process, or required clearances are specified; therefore use a spring-biased inward-opening gate as the provisional interpretation and expose all mechanism dimensions as editable parameters.

Select a plane normal to the intended Y-axis hinge and sketch two symmetric hinge-ear profiles centered on the measured hook-root location immediately behind the hook throat. Use rounded ear profiles with sufficient radial wall around a provisional 2 mm pin bore; make the ear outside radius at least two times the pin radius or increase it after strength review. Position the axis so the closed gate spans the mouth while its inward opening sweep clears the radius-3 mm throat. Keep the ears behind the load-bearing concave seat and avoid cutting faces 7, 8, and 10.

Extrude and unite the hinge-ear profiles locally with the existing hook root, placing one ear on each side of y=0. Minimize lateral growth and keep the additions symmetric so the principal load path remains centered. Provide a central gate space equal to the future gate width plus two provisional running clearances of 0.20 mm. Blend each ear into the spine/hook root with tangent fillets sized from the available local wall, without extending those blends into the load-bearing hook pocket.

Create one coaxial transverse bore through both new hinge ears, with its axis parallel to Y and centered on the hinge construction axis. Use a provisional 2 mm nominal pin diameter, applying manufacturing clearance only after material and process are selected. The subtraction must remain confined to the added ear material and must not intersect the radius-3 mm hook throat or materially reduce the original tapered spine.

operations_plan.summary: Add a shallow gate seat and retaining shoulder to the existing terminal nose without reducing the load-bearing hook bowl.

steps.description: With the gate conceptually in its closed position, project the hinge axis and hook-mouth line onto the XZ mid-plane. Locate the gate contact point on the inward-facing side of the terminal retaining nose, above the primary radius-3 mm load seat and below the horizontal cap at z=15 mm. Set the closed gate to overlap the open-mouth silhouette sufficiently to prevent a carried member from passing between the gate and nose.

Create a small symmetric retaining shoulder on the inward side of the nose, preferably as an additive boss blended into the nose rather than a deep cut. Shape its contact surface to accept the gate tip and resist outward opening while allowing the spring-biased gate to cam inward during loading. Keep the shoulder centered about y=0, within the existing approximate y=±3 mm nose width where practical, and maintain a substantial ligament to the radius-3 mm semicylindrical nose exterior.

Fillet the shoulder-to-nose junction and round the gate-entry edge to form a lead-in cam. Leave the opposing edge comparatively defined so it acts as a positive closed-position stop. Verify that these local blends do not encroach on the existing radius-3 mm seating surface and do not lower the top cap or weaken the radius-9 mm outer hook body.

operations_plan.summary: Create a separate pivoting gate that closes the hook mouth and engages the new retaining shoulder.

steps.description: Create a new component/solid for the gate and sketch its longitudinal profile on the XZ mid-plane. Constrain the root around the hinge axis established in operation_001 and constrain the free end to seat against the retaining shoulder from operation_002. Use a straight or slightly bowed profile that spans the hook opening in the closed position but remains outside the original radius-3 mm load pocket. Use a provisional 2 mm gate depth in the XZ profile, increasing it if later load analysis requires.

Extrude the gate profile symmetrically about y=0 as a separate solid. Set its Y width from the measured spacing between the hinge ears minus two provisional 0.20 mm side clearances. Keep the gate laterally contained within or close to the existing hook-tip width to preserve the overall envelope.

Cut a transverse pivot bore through the gate root concentric with the two hinge-ear bores. Use the same provisional 2 mm nominal pin interface and assign the fit according to the selected manufacturing method: the gate bore should rotate freely while the pin is retained by the stationary ears or by end heads.

Form the gate-tip latch geometry complementary to the nose shoulder. Add a rounded cam surface on the inward-opening side and a short stop surface that bears against the shoulder when closed. Provide local clearance from the semicylindrical nose face 13 and top cap face 17 so the gate does not bind. Round exposed gate edges and add a root fillet around the pivot boss while retaining adequate radial material around the bore.

operations_plan.summary: Add the hinge pin and a compact closing bias so the gate returns to and remains in the secured position.

steps.description: Create a separate cylindrical hinge pin coaxial with the three aligned bores. Use the provisional 2 mm nominal diameter and size its length to span both ears and the gate with minimal axial clearance. Add low-profile heads, upset ends, retaining grooves, or another manufacturable axial-retention detail selected after the production method is known; do not allow the retention detail to interfere with adjacent hook surfaces.

Provide a torsion-spring space around the hinge axis between one hinge ear and the gate, or model an equivalent compact spring element as a separate component. Create one reaction seat on the stationary hinge support and one on the gate root. Orient the spring preload to rotate the gate toward the terminal nose. Spring wire diameter, coil count, material, and torque remain unresolved because no material, cycle-life, or operating-force requirements were supplied.

Assemble the gate, pin, and spring concentrically with the stationary hinge ears. Constrain the pin to the body, allow the gate one rotational degree of freedom about Y, and apply the closed-position stop at the nose shoulder. Set the opening direction inward toward the hook bowl so an entering carried member can push the gate open but an outward-moving member is opposed by the shoulder and spring bias.

operations_plan.summary: Validate motion, retention, preserved geometry, and local manufacturability; then finalize edge treatments.

steps.description: Run an interference and swept-volume check from fully closed to the required loading angle. Confirm that the gate clears both hinge ears, the hook throat, the retaining nose, and the spring throughout rotation. Preserve positive side clearance and ensure the gate can open far enough for the intended carried member; the required member diameter is unresolved and must be supplied before production release.

In the closed position, verify that the gate and nose overlap in the XZ hook-mouth projection, that there is no direct escape path for the carried member, and that outward gate motion is stopped by the retaining shoulder rather than solely by spring force. Confirm that the gate does not occupy or materially reduce the original radius-3 mm load-supporting pocket.

Check minimum wall thickness around the hinge bores, retaining shoulder, and existing nose against the eventual material and load rating. Apply final small chamfers to pin-entry edges and non-contact gate edges, and use generous tangent fillets at added body features. Do not alter the rear clevis slot, radius-3 mm coaxial clevis bores, radius-7.5 mm rounded lugs, or the overall taper and thickness of the long spine beyond the localized hinge-support blend.
